Al-Masudi.subject: Indian Languages
Al-Masudi.question: The _____ was 10th-century Arab historian and geographer.
Al-Masudi.fact: al-Masʿūdī (full name Abū al-Ḥasan ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿAlī al-Masʿūdī, أبو الحسن علي بن الحسين بن علي المسعودي), c. 896–956, was a historian, geographer and traveler sometimes called the "Herodotus of the Arabs".

Al-Masudi.subject: Indian Languages
Al-Masudi.question: 896–956, was a historian, geographer and traveler sometimes referred to as the "_____ of the Arabs"
Al-Masudi.fact: 896–956, was a historian, geographer and traveler sometimes called the "Herodotus of the Arabs".

Al-Masudi.subject: Indian Languages
Al-Masudi.question: Born in _____, he was descended from Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, a companion of Islamic prophet Muhammad
Al-Masudi.fact: Born in Baghdad, he was descended from Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, a companion of Islamic prophet Muhammad.

Al-Masudi.subject: Indian Languages
Al-Masudi.question: It is believed that he was a member of _____ tribe of Arabs
Al-Masudi.fact: It is believed that he was a member of Banu Hudhayl tribe of Arabs.

Al-Masudi.subject: Indian Languages
Al-Masudi.question: His journeys took him to most of the _____ provinces, Armenia, Georgia and other region of the Caspian Sea; as well as to Arabia, Syria and Egypt
Al-Masudi.fact: His journeys took him to most of the Persian provinces, Armenia, Georgia and other region of the Caspian Sea; as well as to Arabia, Syria and Egypt. Al-Masʿudi may have reached Sri Lanka and China although he is known to have met Abu Zayd al-Sirafi on the coast of the Persian Gulf and received information on China from him.

Al-Masudi.subject: Indian Languages
Al-Masudi.question: He also travelled to the _____, and other parts of India, especially the western coast; and he voyaged more than once to East Africa
Al-Masudi.fact: He also travelled to the Indus Valley, and other parts of India, especially the western coast; and he voyaged more than once to East Africa.

Al-Masudi.subject: Indian Languages
Al-Masudi.question: He also sailed on the _____, the Red Sea, the Mediterranean and the Caspian
Al-Masudi.fact: He also sailed on the Indian Ocean, the Red Sea, the Mediterranean and the Caspian.

Al-Masudi.subject: Indian Languages
Al-Masudi.question: Al-Masʿudi may have reached _____ and China although he is known to have met Abu Zayd al-Sirafi on the coast of the Persian Gulf and received information on China from him
Al-Masudi.fact: Al-Masʿudi may have reached Sri Lanka and China although he is known to have met Abu Zayd al-Sirafi on the coast of the Persian Gulf and received information on China from him.

Al-Masudi.subject: Indian Languages
Al-Masudi.question: He presumably gathered information on _____ from the Byzantine admiral, Leo of Tripoli, a convert-to-Islam whom he met in Syria where his last years were divided between there and Egypt
Al-Masudi.fact: He presumably gathered information on Byzantium from the Byzantine admiral, Leo of Tripoli, a convert-to-Islam whom he met in Syria where his last years were divided between there and Egypt.

Al-Masudi.subject: Indian Languages
Al-Masudi.question: In Egypt he found a copy of a _____ king list from Clovis to Louis IV that had been written by an Andalusian bishop
Al-Masudi.fact: In Egypt he found a copy of a Frankish king list from Clovis to Louis IV that had been written by an Andalusian bishop.

Al-Masudi.subject: Indian Languages
Al-Masudi.question: Little is known of his means and funding of his extensive travels within and beyond the lands of _____, and it has been speculated that like many travelers he was involved in trade
Al-Masudi.fact: He presumably gathered information on Byzantium from the Byzantine admiral, Leo of Tripoli, a convert-to-Islam whom he met in Syria where his last years were divided between there and Egypt. Little is known of his means and funding of his extensive travels within and beyond the lands of Islam, and it has been speculated that like many travelers he was involved in trade.

Al-Masudi.subject: Indian Languages
Al-Masudi.question: We know that al-Masʿudi wrote a revised edition of Murūj al-_____ in 956 CE; however, only a draft version from 947 is extant
Al-Masudi.fact: We know that al-Masʿudi wrote a revised edition of Murūj al-Dhahab in 956 CE; however, only a draft version from 947 is extant. Al-Masʿudi in his Tanbīh states that the revised edition of Murūj al-Dhahab contained 365 chapters.

Al-Masudi.subject: Indian Languages
Al-Masudi.question: Al-Masʿudi in his Tanbīh states that the revised edition of Murūj al-_____ contained 365 chapters
Al-Masudi.fact: We know that al-Masʿudi wrote a revised edition of Murūj al-Dhahab in 956 CE; however, only a draft version from 947 is extant. Al-Masʿudi in his Tanbīh states that the revised edition of Murūj al-Dhahab contained 365 chapters.

Al-Masudi.subject: Indian Languages
Al-Masudi.question: Major cities like _____ had large public libraries and many individuals, such as as-Suli, a friend of al-Mas‘udi's, had private libraries, often containing thousands of volumes
Al-Masudi.fact: Major cities like Baghdad had large public libraries and many individuals, such as as-Suli, a friend of al-Mas‘udi's, had private libraries, often containing thousands of volumes.

Al-Masudi.subject: Indian Languages
Al-Masudi.question: Early in the _____ era the art of papermaking was brought to the Islamic world by Chinese prisoners after the battle of Talas and most large towns and cities had paper mills
Al-Masudi.fact: Early in the Abbasid era the art of papermaking was brought to the Islamic world by Chinese prisoners after the battle of Talas and most large towns and cities had paper mills.

Al-Masudi.subject: Indian Languages
Al-Masudi.question: Al-Mas'udi was a pupil, or junior colleague, of prominent intellectuals, including the philologists al-Zajjaj, _____, Niftawayh and ibn Anbari
Al-Masudi.fact: Al-Mas'udi was a pupil, or junior colleague, of prominent intellectuals, including the philologists al-Zajjaj, Ibn Duraid, Niftawayh and ibn Anbari.

Al-Masudi.subject: Indian Languages
Al-Masudi.question: He was acquainted with famous poets, including _____, whom he probably met in Aleppo
Al-Masudi.fact: He was acquainted with famous poets, including Kashajim, whom he probably met in Aleppo.

Al-Masudi.subject: Indian Languages
Al-Masudi.question: He was well read in philosophy, the works of al-Kindi and al-Razi, the _____ thought of al-Farabi and the Platonic writings
Al-Masudi.fact: He was well read in philosophy, the works of al-Kindi and al-Razi, the Aristotelian thought of al-Farabi and the Platonic writings.

Al-Masudi.subject: Indian Languages
Al-Masudi.question: It is probable that al-Masʿudi met al-Razi and al-_____, but only a meeting with al-Farabi's pupil Yahya ibn Adi, of whom he spoke highly, is recorded
Al-Masudi.fact: He was well read in philosophy, the works of al-Kindi and al-Razi, the Aristotelian thought of al-Farabi and the Platonic writings. It is probable that al-Masʿudi met al-Razi and al-Farabi, but only a meeting with al-Farabi's pupil Yahya ibn Adi, of whom he spoke highly, is recorded.

Al-Masudi.subject: Indian Languages
Al-Masudi.question: He was familiar with the medical work of Galen, with _____ astronomy, with the geographical work of Marinus and with the studies of Islamic geographers and astronomers
Al-Masudi.fact: He was familiar with the medical work of Galen, with Ptolemaic astronomy, with the geographical work of Marinus and with the studies of Islamic geographers and astronomers.

Al-Masudi.subject: Indian Languages
Al-Masudi.question: Then the _____ religion appeared in Byzantium and the centres of learning were eliminated, their vestiges effaced and the edifice of Greek learning was obliterated
Al-Masudi.fact: Then the Christian religion appeared in Byzantium and the centres of learning were eliminated, their vestiges effaced and the edifice of Greek learning was obliterated.

Al-Masudi.subject: Indian Languages
Al-Masudi.question: Everything the ancient _____ had brought to light vanished, and the discoveries of the ancients were altered beyond recognition
Al-Masudi.fact: Everything the ancient Greeks had brought to light vanished, and the discoveries of the ancients were altered beyond recognition.

Al-Masudi.subject: Indian Languages
Al-Masudi.question: According to al-Subki, al-Mas'udi was a student of _____, the leading scholar of the Shafi'ite school
Al-Masudi.fact: According to al-Subki, al-Mas'udi was a student of Ibn Surayj, the leading scholar of the Shafi'ite school. Al-Subki claimed he found al-Mas'udi's notes of Ibn Surayj's lectures.

Al-Masudi.subject: Indian Languages
Al-Masudi.question: Al-Subki claimed he found al-Mas'udi's notes of _____'s lectures
Al-Masudi.fact: According to al-Subki, al-Mas'udi was a student of Ibn Surayj, the leading scholar of the Shafi'ite school. Al-Subki claimed he found al-Mas'udi's notes of Ibn Surayj's lectures.

Al-Masudi.subject: Indian Languages
Al-Masudi.question: Al-Mas'udi also met _____'ites during his stay in Egypt
Al-Masudi.fact: According to al-Subki, al-Mas'udi was a student of Ibn Surayj, the leading scholar of the Shafi'ite school. Al-Mas'udi also met Shafi'ites during his stay in Egypt.

Al-Masudi.subject: Indian Languages
Al-Masudi.question: He met _____ in Baghdad and Aleppo such as Ibn Jabir and Niftawayh; modern scholarship leans toward the view that al-Mas'udi was an adherent of the latter school
Al-Masudi.fact: He met Zahirites in Baghdad and Aleppo such as Ibn Jabir and Niftawayh; modern scholarship leans toward the view that al-Mas'udi was an adherent of the latter school.

Al-Masudi.subject: Indian Languages
Al-Masudi.question: Al-Masʿudi knew leading Mu'tazilites, including al-Jubba, al-Nawbakhti, _____ al-Jurjani and Abu'l-Qasim al-Balkhi al-Ka'bi
Al-Masudi.fact: Al-Masʿudi knew leading Mu'tazilites, including al-Jubba, al-Nawbakhti, Ibn Abdak al-Jurjani and Abu'l-Qasim al-Balkhi al-Ka'bi.

Al-Masudi.subject: Indian Languages
Al-Masudi.question: However, _____ points out that his extant works do not specifically state that he was
Al-Masudi.fact: However, Shboul points out that his extant works do not specifically state that he was.

Al-Masudi.subject: Indian Languages
Al-Masudi.question: Al-Mas'udi included the history of the ancient civilizations that had occupied the land upon which _____ later spread
Al-Masudi.fact: Al-Mas'udi included the history of the ancient civilizations that had occupied the land upon which Islam later spread.

Al-Masudi.subject: Indian Languages
Al-Masudi.question: He mentions the _____, Babylonians, Egyptians and Persians among others
Al-Masudi.fact: He mentions the Assyrians, Babylonians, Egyptians and Persians among others. He is also the only Arab historian to refer (albeit indirectly) to the kingdom of Urartu, when he speaks about the wars between the Assyrians (led by the legendary Queen Semiramis) and Armenians (led by King Ara the Handsome).

Al-Masudi.subject: Indian Languages
Al-Masudi.question: Al-Masʿudi was aware of the influence of ancient _____ on Persia
Al-Masudi.fact: He mentions the Assyrians, Babylonians, Egyptians and Persians among others. Al-Masʿudi was aware of the influence of ancient Babylon on Persia.

Al-Masudi.subject: Indian Languages
Al-Masudi.question: He had access to a wealth of translations by scholars such as Abdullah ibn al-Muqaffa from _____ into Arabic
Al-Masudi.fact: He had access to a wealth of translations by scholars such as Abdullah ibn al-Muqaffa from Middle Persian into Arabic.

Al-Masudi.subject: Indian Languages
Al-Masudi.question: In his travels, he also personally consulted _____ scholars and Zoroastrian priests
Al-Masudi.fact: He had access to a wealth of translations by scholars such as Abdullah ibn al-Muqaffa from Middle Persian into Arabic. In his travels, he also personally consulted Persian scholars and Zoroastrian priests.

Al-Masudi.subject: Indian Languages
Al-Masudi.question: Like other _____ historians, he was unclear on the Achaemenid dynasty, though he knew of Kurush (Cyrus the Great)
Al-Masudi.fact: He had access to a wealth of translations by scholars such as Abdullah ibn al-Muqaffa from Middle Persian into Arabic. Like other Arabic historians, he was unclear on the Achaemenid dynasty, though he knew of Kurush (Cyrus the Great).

Al-Masudi.subject: Indian Languages
Al-Masudi.question: He was much clearer on the more recent dynasties and his estimation of the time between _____ the Great and Ardashir is much more accurately depicted than it is in al-Tabari
Al-Masudi.fact: He was much clearer on the more recent dynasties and his estimation of the time between Alexander the Great and Ardashir is much more accurately depicted than it is in al-Tabari. Again, like other Arabic historians, he was unclear on Greece before the Macedonian dynasty that produced Alexander the Great.

Al-Masudi.subject: Indian Languages
Al-Masudi.question: His wide-ranging interests included the _____ and the Romans
Al-Masudi.fact: His wide-ranging interests included the Greeks and the Romans.

Al-Masudi.subject: Indian Languages
Al-Masudi.question: Again, like other _____ historians, he was unclear on Greece before the Macedonian dynasty that produced Alexander the Great
Al-Masudi.fact: Like other Arabic historians, he was unclear on the Achaemenid dynasty, though he knew of Kurush (Cyrus the Great). Again, like other Arabic historians, he was unclear on Greece before the Macedonian dynasty that produced Alexander the Great.

Al-Masudi.subject: Indian Languages
Al-Masudi.question: He also seems unfamiliar with such additional aspects of Greek political life as _____ democratic institutions
Al-Masudi.fact: He also seems unfamiliar with such additional aspects of Greek political life as Athenian democratic institutions.

Al-Masudi.subject: Indian Languages
Al-Masudi.question: The same holds for Rome prior to _____
Al-Masudi.fact: The same holds for Rome prior to Caesar.

Al-Masudi.subject: Indian Languages
Al-Masudi.question: However, he is the earliest extant _____ author to mention the Roman founding myth of Romulus and Remus
Al-Masudi.fact: However, he is the earliest extant Arabic author to mention the Roman founding myth of Romulus and Remus.

Al-Masudi.subject: Indian Languages
Al-Masudi.question: In al-Masʿudi's view the greatest contribution of the _____ was philosophy
Al-Masudi.fact: In al-Masʿudi's view the greatest contribution of the Greeks was philosophy.

Al-Masudi.subject: Indian Languages
Al-Masudi.question: He was aware of the progression of Greek philosophy from the pre-_____ onward
Al-Masudi.fact: He was aware of the progression of Greek philosophy from the pre-Socratics onward.

Al-Masudi.subject: Indian Languages
Al-Masudi.question: He also was keenly interested in the earlier events of the _____ peninsula
Al-Masudi.fact: He also was keenly interested in the earlier events of the Arabian peninsula.

Al-Masudi.subject: Indian Languages
Al-Masudi.question: He recognized that _____ had a long and rich history
Al-Masudi.fact: He also was keenly interested in the earlier events of the Arabian peninsula. He recognized that Arabia had a long and rich history.

Al-Masudi.subject: Indian Languages
Al-Masudi.question: Other authors, even _____ writing in Arabic in the Caliphate, had less to say about the Byzantine Empire than al-Mas'udi
Al-Masudi.fact: Other authors, even Christians writing in Arabic in the Caliphate, had less to say about the Byzantine Empire than al-Mas'udi.

Al-Masudi.subject: Indian Languages
Al-Masudi.question: He also described the geography of many lands beyond the _____, as well as the customs and religious beliefs of many peoples
Al-Masudi.fact: He also described the geography of many lands beyond the Abbasid Caliphate, as well as the customs and religious beliefs of many peoples.

Al-Masudi.subject: Indian Languages
Al-Masudi.question: He perceived the significance of interstate relations and of the interaction of _____ and Hindus in the various states of the subcontinent
Al-Masudi.fact: He perceived the significance of interstate relations and of the interaction of Muslims and Hindus in the various states of the subcontinent.

Al-Masudi.fact: He described previous rulers in China, underlined the importance of the revolt by Huang Chao in the late Tang dynasty, and mentioned, though less detailed than for India, Chinese beliefs.

Al-Masudi.subject: Indian Languages
Al-Masudi.question: His brief portrayal of _____ stands out for its degree of accuracy and clarity
Al-Masudi.fact: His brief portrayal of Southeast Asia stands out for its degree of accuracy and clarity.

Al-Masudi.subject: Indian Languages
Al-Masudi.question: He surveyed the vast areas inhabited by _____ peoples, commenting on what had been the extensive authority of the Khaqan, though this was no longer the case by al-Mas'udi's time
Al-Masudi.fact: He surveyed the vast areas inhabited by Turkic peoples, commenting on what had been the extensive authority of the Khaqan, though this was no longer the case by al-Mas'udi's time. Al-Masudi.subject: Indian Languages

Al-Masudi.fact: He surveyed the vast areas inhabited by Turkic peoples, commenting on what had been the extensive authority of the Khaqan, though this was no longer the case by al-Mas'udi's time. He conveyed the great diversity of Turkic peoples, including the distinction between sedentary and nomadic Turks.

Al-Masudi.question: He spoke of the significance of the _____ and provided much fresh material on them
Al-Masudi.fact: He spoke of the significance of the Khazars and provided much fresh material on them.

Al-Masudi.subject: Indian Languages
Al-Masudi.question: His account of the Rus is an important early source for the study of _____ history and the history of Ukraine
Al-Masudi.fact: His account of the Rus is an important early source for the study of Russian history and the history of Ukraine.

Al-Masudi.fact: Again, while he may have read such earlier Arabic authors as Ibn Khordadbeh, Ibn al-Faqih, ibn Rustah and Ibn Fadlan, al-Mas'udi presented most of his material based on his personal observations and contacts made while traveling. Al-Masudi.fact: He was very well informed on Rus trade with the Byzantines and on the competence of the Rus in sailing merchant vessels and warships. He recorded the effect of the westward migration of various tribes upon the Byzantines, especially the invading Bulgars.

Al-Masudi.fact: He knows Paris as the Frankish capital. He obtained a copy of a list of Frankish rulers from Clovis to his own time.

Al-Masudi.fact: He described the relations of African states with each other and with Islam. He provided material on the cultures and beliefs of non-Islamic Africans.

Al-Masudi.fact: He provided material on the cultures and beliefs of non-Islamic Africans.
